new_statements.quote: [p.50] Cabe anotar que los datos (vea el apéndice) corresponden principalmente a las variedades que se hablan en el departamento de Huánuco, especialmente las variedades de Ambo-Pasco, Margos-Yarowilca-Lauricocha (MYL) y Huamalíes. Las conclusiones del presente trabajo se aplican principalmente a esas variedades [...] [p.52] Se puede saber que en el segundo caso la partícula es ligada por la colocación de la fuerza de la voz que en quechua recae en la penúltima sílaba: a.'li.cag NO 'a.li # cag
new_statements.translation: [p.50] Note that the data (see appendix) come principally from the varieties spoken in the department of Huánuco, especially Ambo-Pasco, Margos-Yarowilca-Lauricocha (MYL) and Huamalíes. The conclusions of this study apply principally to those varieties [...] [p.52] One can tell that in the second case the particle is bound from the placement of stress ('la fuerza de la voz'), which in Quechua falls on the penultimate syllable: a.'li.cag, NOT 'a.li # cag.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the (phonological) word, so a cliticized/bound element counts toward the penult computation (alicag stressed a.LI.cag).
new_statements.exceptions: None in Toliver. The companion article in the same volume (Weber & Landerman 2008:25-26, general Central Quechua) adds that a word-final long vowel marking 1st person carries stress, and that in Huallaga 'and some other varieties' other word-final long vowels are stressed too; Huamalíes is not named there.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level; used as a diagnostic of word-hood (bound vs free particle). The remark is a pooled generalization over the author's Huánuco data (Ambo-Pasco, MYL, Huamalíes); the illustrating form is written in Ambo-Pasco orthography, so it is not a Huamalíes-specific description. The dedicated description of this variety (Solá 1967, Llata) was not accessible.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement (Toliver 2008:52) is a pooled generalization over the author's Huánuco corpus, which he says comes 'principalmente' from Ambo-Pasco (qva, ambo1252), Margos-Yarowilca-Lauricocha (qvm, marg1254) and Huamalíes (qvh, huam1248); the illustrating word is in Ambo-Pasco orthography. It is therefore evidence for huam1248 only by inclusion, not a Huamalíes-specific description. The dedicated description of this variety is Solá 1967 (based on Llata, capital of Huamalíes = Glottolog dialect huam1249), not accessible. Cancino 2019 describes La Unión (Dos de Mayo) Quechua, which Cerrón-Palomino's 'Alto Marañón' grouping and Domínguez 2006 place with Huamalíes, but it is silent on stress.

sources.citation: Weber, David J. & Peter N. Landerman. 2008. La interpretación de las vocales largas en el quechua. In Coombs & Bergli (eds.), Estudios quechuas II (SLP 55), 12-28. Lima: ILV.
sources.note: pp.25-26: 'En la mayoría de las variedades centrales del quechua, el acento se asigna a la penúltima sílaba'; word-final long vowel marking 1st person is stressed; in Huallaga 'y algunas otras variedades' other final long vowels also stressed; some Ancash varieties initial stress + final-heavy in utterance-final word. General Central Quechua, no variety named Huamalíes.

sources.citation: Weber, David J. 1996 [2008 digital ed.]. Una gramática del quechua del Huallaga (Huánuco). Serie Lingüística Peruana 40. Lima: ILV.
sources.note: Huallaga (qub), not qvh: §23.6 p.590 'El acento se asigna básicamente a la penúltima mora' (penult syllable normally; word-final long vowels stressed). Mentions Huamalíes/Llata only for morphology, citing Solá 1967 [ref 45] as the description of 'el quechua de Llata (Huánuco)'.

sources.citation: Parker, Gary J. 1971. Comparative Quechua Phonology and Grammar V: The Evolution of Quechua B. Working Papers in Linguistics (Hawaii) 3(3). [ERIC microfiche scanned]
sources.note: Assumes Proto-Quechua-B 'rule of penultimate syllable accent'; mentions 'my own scant data for Huamalíes' (Llata) for segmental isoglosses only; no lect-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Julca Guerrero, Félix (chapter 'Quechua de Áncash') in Zariquiey, R. et al. (eds.) 2024. Enciclopedia de las lenguas indígenas u originarias del Perú en el Bicentenario, vol. 1. Lima: Ministerio de Cultura / PUCP.
sources.note: Treats Huamalíes, Huacaybamba and parts of Dos de Mayo as affiliated with Conchucos/Ancash Quechua; notes /q/ voicing to [g] in Huamalíes; cites Howard 2014 'El quechua de Huamalíes' (unpublished ponencia). No Huamalíes stress statement seen.

sources.note: §4.2 Fonología pp.100-102 (La Unión, Dos de Mayo): 27 phonemes plus one suprasegmental, 'la duración /:/'; no statement on stress; author says no prior phonological description of this variety exists.
